interpretation: CLAP scores acoustic descriptions. The sound-to-geometry correspondences below are proposed experiment controls, not Livia's own claims or decoded animal meanings.

descriptors.text: The sound of a series of short dry clicks.
descriptors.material: a rhythm of repeated open cells in cast sterling-silver ribs, interrupted by small clear gaps, with an exposed amber core
descriptors.edit: repeat a few small open cells along the existing silver rim, keeping the amber face exposed
descriptors.connection: Nanot of Power's open silver lattice; repeated modules become structural bays in Livistone.

descriptors.text: The sound of a sustained high-pitched whistle.
descriptors.material: long continuous curved cast sterling-silver ribbons flowing around a visible amber core, generous open gaps between the ribbons
descriptors.edit: lengthen and smooth the existing silver folds into continuous curved ribbons around the amber
descriptors.connection: Mitoring's silver folds and Ammonite's curved setting; continuous strands can become walkable architectural edges.

descriptors.text: The sound of a slowly wavering tonal sound.
descriptors.material: gently undulating folded cast sterling-silver ribs around a visible amber core, with open channels between the folds
descriptors.edit: give the existing silver folds a gentle undulation and open small channels between them
descriptors.connection: Mitoring's crista-like folds and Mycelium's open drainage network; Livistone turns these structures into an energy hall and rain garden.
